verses.1:1: The burden of the word of the Lord concerning Israel, by the hand of His messenger; lay it now upon your hearts.
verses.1:2: "I have loved you," says the Lord. Yet you said, "In what have You loved us?" "Was not Esau the brother of Jacob?" says the Lord. "Yet I loved Jacob,
verses.1:3: but Esau I hated; and I appointed his borders to desolation, and his inheritance to gifts of the wilderness."
verses.1:4: Because one will say, "Idumea has been overthrown, so let us return and rebuild the desolate places," thus says the Lord Almighty: "They shall build, and I will tear down; and they shall be called Borders of Lawlessness, and the people against whom the Lord stands arrayed forever.
verses.1:5: And your eyes shall see, and you shall say, 'The Lord has been magnified above the borders of Israel.'"
verses.1:6: "A son glorifies his father, and a servant his master. And if I am a Father, where is My glory? And if I am a Master, where is My fear?" says the Lord Almighty. "You are the priests who despise My name!" Yet you said, "In what have we despised Your name?"
verses.1:7: "By bringing defiled loaves to My altar." Yet you said, "In what have we defiled them?" "By your saying, 'The table of the Lord is defiled,' and you have held in contempt the things set upon it.
verses.1:8: For if you bring the blind for a sacrifice, is it not evil? And if you bring the lame or the sick, is it not evil? Present it now to your governor: will he accept you, or will he regard your person?" says the Lord Almighty.
verses.1:9: And now, appease the face of your God and plead with Him. "By your hands these things have been done; will I accept your persons from among you?" says the Lord Almighty.
verses.1:10: "Because even among you the doors shall be shut, and My altar shall not be kindled in vain. I have no delight in you," says the Lord Almighty, "nor will I accept a sacrifice from your hands.
verses.1:11: For from the rising of the sun even to its setting, My name has been glorified among the nations; and in every place incense is offered to My name, and a pure sacrifice; for My name is great among the nations," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.1:12: "But you profane it by your saying, 'The table of the Lord is defiled, and what is laid upon it, even His food, is held in contempt.'"
verses.1:13: And you said, "These things are from weariness!" "And I blew them away," says the Lord Almighty. "Yet you brought in plundered things, and the lame, and the afflicted; and if you bring the sacrifice, will I accept them from your hands?" says the Lord Almighty.
verses.1:14: "And cursed is the one who had the means, and there was a male in his flock, and his vow was upon it, yet he sacrifices what is blemished to the Lord. For I am a great King," says the Lord Almighty, "and My name is illustrious among the nations."
verses.2:1: "And now, this commandment is for you, O priests.
verses.2:2: If you will not listen, and if you will not take it to heart to give glory to My name," says the Lord Almighty, "then I will send out the curse upon you, and I will curse your blessing—indeed, I will curse it; and I will scatter your blessing, and it shall not be among you, because you do not take it to heart.
verses.2:3: Behold, I separate the shoulder from you, and I will scatter the maw upon your faces, the maw of the feasts, and I will take you away to the same place;
verses.2:4: and you shall know that I have sent forth this commandment to you, that My covenant may be with the Levites," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.2:5: "My covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I gave it to him that he might fear with fear, and stand in awe before My name.
verses.2:6: The law of truth was in his mouth, and unrighteousness was not found upon his lips; keeping a straight path in peace, he walked with Me, and turned many away from unrighteousness.
verses.2:7: For the lips of a priest shall guard knowledge, and they shall seek the law from his mouth; because he is a messenger of the Lord Almighty.
verses.2:8: But you have turned aside from the way and have weakened many in the law; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi?" says the Lord Almighty.
verses.2:9: "And I also have made you despised and cast out among all the nations, because you do not keep My ways, but showed partiality in the law."
verses.2:10: Has not one God created you? Is there not one Father of you all? Why is it that each of you has forsaken his brother, to profane the covenant of your fathers?
verses.2:11: Judah has been forsaken, and an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah has profaned the holy things of the Lord, in that he loved and devoted himself to foreign gods.
verses.2:12: The Lord will utterly destroy the man who does these things, even until he is humbled out of the tents of Jacob, and from among those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord Almighty.
verses.2:13: "And these things which I hated, you did: you covered the altar of the Lord with tears, with weeping and groaning from troubles. Is it still fitting to look upon a sacrifice, or to receive what is acceptable from your hands?"
verses.2:14: And you said, "For what reason?" Because the Lord has borne witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you have forsaken; yet she is your companion and the wife of your covenant.
verses.2:15: And did He not make what is good, and a remnant of His Spirit? And you said, "What else does God seek except offspring?" Therefore guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not forsake the wife of your youth.
verses.2:16: "But if in hatred you send her away," says the Lord, the God of Israel, "then ungodliness shall cover your thoughts," says the Lord Almighty. Therefore guard yourselves in your spirit, and by no means forsake her,
verses.2:17: you who provoke God with your words! Yet you said, "In what have we provoked Him?" By your saying, "Everyone who does evil is good in the sight of the Lord, and in them He Himself is well pleased," and, "Where is the God of justice?"
verses.3:1: "Behold, I am sending forth My messenger, and he shall survey the way before My face; and suddenly the Lord whom you seek shall come into His own temple, and the Messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Behold, He is coming," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.3:2: And who shall endure the day of His entrance? Or who shall stand firm at His appearing? For He enters like the fire of a smelting furnace, and like the lye of fullers.
verses.3:3: He shall sit smelting and purifying as with silver and as with gold; and He shall purify the sons of Levi and refine them just as gold and as silver; and they shall bring to the Lord a sacrifice in righteousness,
verses.3:4: and the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem shall be pleasing to the Lord, as in the days of old and as in the former years.
verses.3:5: "And I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against the sorceresses, and against the adulteresses, and against those who swear falsely by My name, and against those who defraud the hired laborer of his wages, and those who oppress a widow, and those who beat orphans with the fist, and those who turn aside the judgment of a proselyte, and those who do not fear Me," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.3:6: "For I am the Lord your God, and I have not changed.
verses.3:7: And you, O sons of Jacob, do not abstain from the unrighteous deeds of your fathers; you have turned aside from My ordinances and have not kept them. Return to Me, and I will return to you," says the Lord, the Almighty. And you said, "In what shall we return?"
verses.3:8: "Will a man cheat God? For you are cheating Me." Yet you shall say, "In what have we cheated You?" "Because the tithes and the firstfruits are with you;
verses.3:9: and looking away, you look away, and it is Me you cheat.
verses.3:10: The year has been completed, and you have brought all the produce into the storehouses, and his plunder shall be in his house. Examine now in this matter," says the Lord Almighty, "whether I will not open for you the floodgates of heaven, and pour out My blessing for you until there is enough.
verses.3:11: And I will allot for you for food, and I will by no means destroy the fruit of your ground, nor shall your vine in the field fail," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.3:12: "And all the nations shall call you blessed, for you yourselves shall be a desired land," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.3:13: "You have made your words heavy against Me," says the Lord. Yet you said, "In what have we spoken against You?"
verses.3:14: You said, "Vain is the one who serves God; and what profit is it that we have kept His charges, and that we have walked as suppliants before the face of the Lord Almighty?
verses.3:15: And now we call foreigners blessed; and all who do lawless things are built up; indeed, they have withstood God and have been delivered."
verses.3:16: These things those who fear the Lord spoke, each one to his neighbor; and the Lord paid heed and listened, and He wrote a book of remembrance before Him for those who fear the Lord and revere His name.
verses.3:17: "And they shall be Mine," says the Lord Almighty, "on the day which I make, for a treasured possession; and I will choose them in the manner in which a man chooses his own son who serves him.
verses.3:18: And you shall return and discern between the righteous and the lawless, and between the one who serves God and the one who does not serve.
verses.3:19: For behold, a day is coming, burning like a furnace, and it shall burn them; and all the foreigners and all who do lawless things shall be stubble, and the coming day shall set them ablaze," says the Lord Almighty, "and neither root nor branch shall be left of them.
verses.3:20: And for you who fear My name, the Sun of righteousness shall rise, and healing is in His wings; and you shall go forth and leap like calves loosed from their bonds.
verses.3:21: And you shall trample down the lawless, for they shall be ashes beneath your feet on the day which I make," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.3:22: "And behold, I am sending to you Elijah the Tishbite before the great and notable day of the Lord comes,
verses.3:23: who shall restore the heart of a father to a son, and the heart of a man to his neighbor, lest I come and strike the earth utterly."
verses.3:24: "Remember the law of Moses My servant, just as I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel, statutes and ordinances."

notes.1:1: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew title as an appellative, "His messenger" (angelou autou), rather than the proper name Malachi, and adds the closing exhortation "lay it now upon your hearts."
notes.1:3: The Greek reads "gifts of the wilderness" (domata eremou), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants rendered "jackals of the wilderness" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.1:4: The Septuagint uses the Greek name "Idumea" for Edom and renders the final verb as a military term ("stands arrayed," paratetaktai) rather than "has indignation."
notes.1:13: The Greek uses a first-person singular verb ("I blew them away," exephysesa), expressing the Lord's own rejection of the offerings, rather than the second-person "you sneer at it" of the Masoretic Text.
notes.1:14: The Septuagint reads "the one who had the means" (dynatos) rather than "the deceiver."
notes.2:3: The Greek reads "the shoulder" (omon) rather than "the seed" and "the maw" (enystron, the ruminant's stomach) rather than "dung," recalling the priestly portions prescribed in Deuteronomy 18:3.
notes.2:11: The Septuagint reads passively "Judah has been forsaken" and describes Judah as having "devoted himself to foreign gods" rather than marrying the daughter of a foreign god.
notes.2:15: In this notoriously difficult verse, the Greek reads "did He not make what is good" (ou kalon epoiesen) rather than "did He not make them one" and attributes the following question directly to the people ("And you said").
notes.2:16: Rather than "I hate divorce," the Septuagint reads a second-person condition ("if in hatred you send her away") and warns that ungodliness shall cover "your thoughts" (enthymemata) rather than "his garment."
notes.3:6: The Septuagint ends verse 6 after "I have not changed" and begins verse 7 with "And you, O sons of Jacob, do not abstain from the unrighteous deeds of your fathers," differing from the Masoretic verse division and reading ("you are not consumed").
notes.3:8: The Greek verb pternizo ("trip up by the heel," "supplant," here rendered "cheat") echoes the wordplay on Jacob's name in Genesis 27:36, reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew verb usually rendered "rob."
notes.3:10: The Septuagint opens verse 10 with "The year has been completed," uses a past-tense verb ("you have brought"), and reads "his plunder shall be in his house" rather than "that there may be food in My house."
notes.3:22: In the Septuagint, Malachi concludes within chapter 3 (verses 19-24 correspond to 4:1-6 in English Bibles), placing the promise of Elijah (3:22-23) before the command to remember the law of Moses (3:24); in 3:23 the Greek also reads "the heart of a man to his neighbor" rather than "the hearts of the children to their fathers."
